coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app's riskiest logic — data transformation, filtering, pagination, URL state, caching — is entirely untested; the only guard is the external acceptance suite.

behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests at all, so nothing asserts observable behaviour either; per the rubric, 'no tests' scores 1.

app/src/components/moves-table.tsx:35 — missing-values-sort-last and aria-sort toggle unguarded

regression_power.rationale: With no tests inside app/, a refactor of the data layer or filter logic would pass every check the repo itself owns; only the external, non-run-in-app acceptance suite would notice.

evidence: app/ — no tests, hence no noise
signal_to_noise.rationale: Rubric default for no tests: 3. There is no padding to criticize, but nothing earning its keep either.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no test script, no vitest/playwright dependency, no spec files anywhere in app/.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (Qwik 1.x's documented unit-test runner) plus a `test` script, and unit-test app/src/lib/format.ts, urls.ts and api.ts — they are plain functions with the highest logic density.

findings.issue: cardsForPokemonRefs implements the trickiest business rule (Pokémon→species mapping, alternate-form exclusion at pokemonId >= 10000, dedup, hidden-ability flag) with no tests; a refactor silently breaks move/ability/type card lists.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with fixture refs covering: default Pokémon, ID ≥ 10000 exclusion, duplicate species, fallback fetch path, and hidden-flag propagation.

findings.issue: Search/type/generation filtering, page clamping and the 48-per-page slice are unguarded; off-by-one pagination or slot-matching regressions would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Extract the loader's filter/slice logic into a pure function in app/src/lib/ and test edge cases (empty q, page > totalPages, page=abc, type in slot 2 only).

findings.issue: homeUrl's omit-empty/default parameter rule and the implicit reset-to-page-1 when a filter changes (callers at app/src/routes/index.tsx:110-124 drop `page`) are untested.
findings.suggestion: Property-style unit tests: page 1 omitted, empty q omitted, combined filters preserved in order.

findings.issue: Moves grouping (dedup key `${move}|${level}` may merge distinct learn entries), method ordering, default game = last-by-order, and per-method row sorting are all untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract the version-group selection and table-building into pure functions and test with a small moves fixture, including a move learned at two levels.

findings.issue: Client-side sort comparator (missing values last in both directions, stability tiebreak, aria-sort toggling) has only light acceptance coverage.
findings.suggestion: Test compareValues directly (null vs number/string, both directions) plus a Playwright interaction test for second-click descending.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled concurrency limiter (waiter queue/active accounting) and promise cache with rejected-promise eviction can deadlock or cache failures if refactored; fan-outs in getTypes/getGenerations depend on it (app/src/lib/data.ts:18,30).
findings.suggestion: Unit tests that push > MAX_CONCURRENT requests, force a rejection, and assert all resolve and the entry is retried.

findings.issue: Non-404 API failures throw out of loaders; the user-facing behaviour of an API outage is undefined and untested.
findings.suggestion: Decide and test an error path (retry or a friendly error page) so a 500/timeout doesn't surface as a framework stack trace.

findings.issue: Not-found behavior, including per-route 404s and lowercase name normalization (app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:20), is only covered by external acceptance tests.
findings.suggestion: Keep one route-level Playwright test inside app/ for the 404 path and a case-variant URL so casing regressions are caught.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own — no test script, no runner, not even a placeholder — and relies entirely on the external acceptance suite for correctness. The unguarded surface includes the highest-risk logic in the codebase: Pokémon→species mapping, the filter/pagination pipeline, URL-state construction, moves grouping, client-side sorting, and a hand-rolled fetch limiter/cache. Extracting that logic into pure functions and covering it with Vitest would be a small, high-leverage addition before this codebase is handed to a team.

untested.area: API failure handling beyond 404 (app/src/lib/api.ts:38-39 throws; no error boundary or retry)
